mainTopic: Wool that fell off a blemished בכור before it died or was slaughtered: the מחלוקת between עקביא בן מהללאל and the חכמים, as reported by רבי יהודה and by רבי יוסי, plus the rule for wool that is only half-detached.
overview: The משנה finishes רבי יהודה's version of an argument between עקביא בן מהללאל and the חכמים about hair that fell off a blemished בכור before it was slaughtered. רבי יוסי says the argument was really about a בכור that died. The משנה then rules on wool that is only dangling from the animal. The גמרא explains that in רבי יוסי's view everyone permits the wool when the animal was slaughtered, and ריש לקיש adds that the argument applies only where a מומחה had permitted the animal. רב ששת challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא about blemished animals mixed into a flock, where רבי יוסי says "יבקר." רב נחמן reads that ברייתא as being about mixed wool, and רבא defends ריש לקיש. In ארץ ישראל, רבי ירמיה rejects this reading and brings two versions of רבי יוחנן: the argument is about searching and not finding the blemished animal, or about searching and finding it. Each version is tied to an older argument about lost טומאה. The amud ends as the גמרא starts a new challenge to ריש לקיש from wool plucked off an unblemished בכור, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages forbid it, in רבי יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes רבי יהודה's report: in the case of fallen hair from a blemished בכור that was later slaughtered, עקביא permits it and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages forbid it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a sentence from the משנה just before it. There, עקביא בן מהללאל permits hair that fell off a blemished בכור and was set aside before the animal was slaughtered. Here we are told the חכמים forbid it, and that this is רבי יהודה's report of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור that has a blemish may be slaughtered and used, and so may its wool. The question is whether hair that fell off earlier, while using it was still forbidden, becomes permitted once the animal is slaughtered. According to רבי יהודה, עקביא says yes and the חכמים say no.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal that is holy

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new case. It is the end of a sentence that began in the משנה just before it, about hair that fell off and was set aside before the animal was slaughtered.

phrases.english: and the Sages forbid it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's sentence that began in the text just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the חכמים forbid fallen hair from a blemished בכור even after the animal is slaughtered, while עקביא permits it.

steps.title: רבי יוסי moves the argument to a case where the animal died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the argument between עקביא and the חכמים was not about a slaughtered animal. It was about a blemished בכור whose fallen hair was set aside and which then died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: It was not in that case that עקביא בן מהללאל permitted it. Rather, in the case of hair from a blemished animal that fell off, which a person put in a window, and afterward the animal died: in that case עקביא בן מהללאל permits it and the Sages forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with how רבי יהודה reported the argument. He says the real case was one where the animal died, not one where it was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור that dies without being slaughtered must be buried, and so must the hair still attached to it. So the question becomes harder: once the animal has died, may the hair that fell off earlier be used? In רבי יוסי's version, עקביא permits it and the חכמים forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not in this case that he permitted it
A window or wall opening used as a storage spot

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא's question in the next steps is based on the exact wording רבי יוסי uses here: "not in this case."

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל,
phrases.english: it was not in this case that Akavya ben Mahalalel permitted it,
phrases.notes: "This case" means רבי יהודה's case, where the animal was slaughtered.

phrases.english: rather, hair of a blemished animal that fell off
and he put it in a window, and afterward the animal died:
in this case Akavya ben Mahalalel permits it
and the Sages forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's report and moves the argument to a different case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the argument is about fallen hair from a blemished בכור that later died: עקביא permits it and the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: Wool that is still dangling from a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: Wool that is half-detached and looks like part of the fleece counts as part of the fleece and is permitted. Wool that does not look like part of the fleece is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wool that is dangling from a firstborn: the part that looks like it belongs with the fleece is permitted, and the part that does not look like it belongs with the fleece is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule about wool that has not fully fallen off a בכור but is hanging loose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a blemished בכור is slaughtered, its fleece may be sheared and used. Loose wool that still looks like part of that fleece goes along with it and is permitted. Loose wool that looks separate is treated like hair that already fell off, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The fleece, the wool that gets sheared

steps.whatToRemember: Half-detached wool is judged by how it looks. If it looks like part of the fleece, it is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Wool that is dangling from a firstborn:
what looks like part of the fleece is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה עִם הַגִּיזָּה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and what does not look like part of the fleece is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: צֶמֶר הַמְדוּלְדָּל בַּבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule in the משנה, on a related subject: wool that is only partly detached.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dangling wool that looks like part of the fleece is permitted; dangling wool that does not look like part of the fleece is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's wording seems to imply something that makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's words "not in this case did he permit" seem to mean that עקביא forbids the wool when the animal was slaughtered. But if עקביא permits it even when the animal died, the slaughtered case should obviously be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: That implies he forbids it! Now, if he permits it when the animal died, does he even need to say so when the animal was slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of רבי יוסי in the משנה. That wording seems to say that עקביא forbids the wool in the slaughtered case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case where the animal died is the stricter one, since the animal and its attached hair must be buried. The slaughtered case is the easier one, since the animal and its wool may be used. So if עקביא permits the wool in the harder case, he would surely permit it in the easier case, and it makes no sense to suggest that he forbids it there.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the Sages that analyzes the משנה
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: Gemara: This implies that he forbids it!
phrases.notes: He means: "not in this case did he permit" sounds as if עקביא forbids the wool when the animal was slaughtered.

phrases.english: Now, if when the animal died he permits it,
is it even necessary to say so when he slaughtered it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּאָסַר, הַשְׁתָּא בְּמֵת שָׁרֵי, שְׁחָטוֹ מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבי יוסי's statement in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If עקביא permits the wool in the harder case (the animal died), he must also permit it in the easier case (the animal was slaughtered). So reading רבי יוסי as saying עקביא forbids the slaughtered case makes no sense.

steps.title: Everyone permits it if slaughtered; they argue only if it died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי means that the slaughtered case is not where עקביא and the חכמים argue, because there everyone permits the wool. Their argument is only in the case where the animal died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he means: It was not in this case that עקביא permitted and the Sages forbade. If he slaughtered it, everyone agrees it is permitted. Where they argue is when the animal died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by explaining what רבי יוסי really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Not in this case" does not mean that עקביא forbids the slaughtered case. It means there is no argument there at all, because everyone, even the חכמים, permits the wool. The only argument is about an animal that died.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, if a blemished בכור is slaughtered, everyone permits its earlier fallen wool. עקביא and the חכמים argue only when the animal died.

phrases.english: Rather, it was not in this case that Akavya permitted
and the Sages forbade,
since if he slaughtered it, everyone agrees it is permitted;
where they argue is when it died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4 by explaining רבי יוסי's wording differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: "not in this case" means there is no argument in that case, not that עקביא forbids it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's words seemed to say that עקביא forbids the wool when the animal was slaughtered.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the slaughtered case everyone permits the wool. The argument between עקביא and the חכמים is only when the animal died.

steps.title: The argument applies only when an expert permitted the animal
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says עקביא and the חכמים argue only where an expert had permitted the blemished בכור. One side decrees against the wool so the owner won't delay slaughtering it, and the other side does not. Without an expert's permission, everyone forbids the wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי quotes ריש לקיש: The argument is in a case where an expert permitted the animal. One side says we make a decree, because the owner might put off slaughtering it. The other side says we do not make that decree. But if no expert permitted it, everyone agrees the wool is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש tells us exactly which case the argument between עקביא and the חכמים is about, and gives the reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a מומחה declares the blemish real, the בכור may be slaughtered, so its wool could in principle be permitted. The question is only whether to make a גזירה, because an owner enjoying the fallen wool might keep the animal alive longer. If no מומחה ever permitted it, the wool fell from an animal that was still fully holy, so nobody permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert who examines a blemish and permits the בכור to be slaughtered
We make a rabbinic decree (a protective rule)
To delay it (keep the animal alive longer)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the framework that רב ששת is about to challenge.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi says that Reish Lakish says:
The dispute is where an expert permitted it,
phrases.notes: The expert said the blemish is real, so the בכור may be slaughtered. This happened before the wool fell out.

phrases.english: for one Sage holds: we decree
phrases.notes: This side is the חכמים, who forbid the wool.

phrases.english: lest he come to delay it,
and one Sage holds: we do not decree,
phrases.notes: This side is עקביא, who permits the wool.

phrases.english: but where an expert did not permit it,
all agree it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁהִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows and explains the argument that step 5 placed in the case where the animal died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument applies only where a מומחה permitted the בכור. The issue is a גזירה against delaying slaughter. Without a מומחה, everyone forbids the wool.

steps.title: רב ששת brings a ברייתא about blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת starts a challenge by quoting a ברייתא: blemished animals make a mixture forbidden in any amount, and רבי יוסי says 'let it be checked'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raised an objection: Blemished animals make the whole mix forbidden, no matter how small their share. רבי יוסי says: let it be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. רב ששת quotes a ברייתא, and the actual point of his attack comes after the ברייתא is explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא records two views about a mixture involving something from a בעל מום. The תנא קמא forbids everything, even if the blemished part is tiny. רבי יוסי says 'יבקר', but what that word means is not yet clear.

keyTerms.meaning: In any amount, even the smallest
Let it be checked or investigated

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
Blemished ones make forbidden in any amount,
and Rabbi Yosei says: Let it be checked.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to ריש לקיש's framework in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's statement that without an expert's permission everyone forbids the wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא needs to be explained first (steps 8 and 9). Its full force against ריש לקיש only comes out after that.

steps.title: What does 'let it be checked' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי means by 'יבקר'. If he means find the blemished animal and remove it, that would imply the תנא קמא forbids the rest even after removal, which makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What does 'let it be checked' mean? If you say it means find the blemished one and take it out, then that would imply the first תנא says no, you can't. That can't be right!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to figure out what רבי יוסי's word 'יבקר' means, and shows that the simple reading doesn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'יבקר' meant 'search for the blemished animal and remove it,' then the תנא קמא would be disagreeing. That would mean he forbids the remaining good animals even after the bad one is gone. That position is impossible, so the ברייתא must be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (we raised a question about it)
If you say (introduces a possible reading that will be rejected)
And let him take it out
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What does 'let it be checked' mean?
Shall we say: search for the one that is blemished,
and remove it?
By implication, the first tanna says no?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי ״יְבַקֵּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the key word in the ברייתא from step 7 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוסי means by 'יבקר', given that the simple reading would leave the תנא קמא with an impossible position

steps.title: The ברייתא is about mixed wool, following each side's version
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, explains that the ברייתא is about wool from a blemished בכור mixed into ordinary wool. The תנא קמא is רבי יהודה, who says the חכמים forbid wool even when the animal was slaughtered. רבי יוסי follows his own view that in the slaughtered case the חכמים permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Here we are dealing with wool from a blemished בכור that got mixed into ordinary wool. Who is the first תנא? It is רבי יהודה, who says that when they were slaughtered, the חכמים forbid. And רבי יוסי follows his own reasoning, since he says that when they were slaughtered, the חכמים permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by moving the ברייתא to a new case: mixed wool. Each opinion in the ברייתא matches one of the two versions of the argument from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא is not about live animals but about the wool of a blemished בכור mixed with חולין wool. The תנא קמא forbids the whole mixture because he holds like רבי יהודה (step 1), that the חכמים forbid even a slaughtered animal's wool. רבי יוסי says 'check', because in his version (steps 2 and 5) a slaughtered animal's wool is permitted, so it depends on what happened to the animal.
steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה are not giving their own rulings. Each one is reporting what the חכמים said, and they report it differently (see steps 1-2).
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's argument about mixed wool matches the two versions of the עקביא-חכמים argument. רבי יהודה's version forbids slaughtered wool, and רבי יוסי's version permits it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman says that Rabba bar Avuh says:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּגִיזַּת בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with wool of a blemished firstborn
that became mixed with non-sacred wool.
And who is the first tanna?
It is Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
If they were slaughtered, the Rabbis forbid.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's report in our משנה, back in step 1.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei follows his reasoning, as he says:
If they were slaughtered, the Rabbis permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: הָכָא בְּגִיזַּת בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8 by giving the ברייתא a new case and matching each opinion to a version of the argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is about blemished-בכור wool mixed with חולין wool. The תנא קמא is רבי יהודה (the חכמים forbid slaughtered wool). רבי יוסי follows his own version (the חכמים permit slaughtered wool).

steps.title: רב ששת's challenge: checking means checking the blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת argues that 'יבוקר' means an expert checks whether the blemish is permanent or temporary. That would mean רבי יוסי permits the wool even though no expert permitted the animal beforehand, which goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says 'let it be checked.' What does 'let it be checked' mean? Doesn't it mean we check whether it is a permanent blemish or a temporary blemish, even though no expert permitted it beforehand?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת now finishes the challenge he began in step 7. He reads 'יבוקר' as 'check what kind of blemish it is' and uses that to attack ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said that without an expert's permission, everyone forbids the wool. If רבי יוסי permits wool simply because the blemish later turns out to be permanent, he permits it without any prior expert approval. That contradicts ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be checked or examined
A permanent blemish, which allows a בכור to be slaughtered
A temporary blemish, which does not allow slaughter
An expert who rules on blemishes

phrases.english: And it teaches: "Let it be checked,"
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא רב ששת quoted in step 7, where רבי יוסי said this.

phrases.english: What does "let it be checked" mean?
Is it not: whether it is a "permanent blemish"
or a "temporary blemish,"

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב שֶׁלֹּא הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה.
phrases.english: even though an expert had not permitted it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָתָנֵי: יְבוּקַּר, מַאי יְבוּקַּר? לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge רב ששת started in step 7, now that step 9 has made clear the ברייתא is about wool.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim (step 6) that without an expert's permission, everyone forbids the wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'יבוקר' means checking whether the blemish is permanent, then רבי יוסי permits wool without any prior expert approval.

steps.title: רבא: checking means checking whether an expert permitted it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that 'יבוקר' means we check whether an expert had permitted the בכור. If one had, the wool is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: No. 'Let it be checked' means: if an expert permitted it, yes, the wool is permitted; and if not, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends ריש לקיש by giving 'יבוקר' a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The checking is not about the type of blemish. It is about whether an expert had already permitted the animal. So רבי יוסי also requires an expert's permission, just as ריש לקיש said.

phrases.english: Rava said: No;
"let it be checked": if an expert permitted it, yes,
phrases.notes: Yes means the mixed-in wool is permitted.

phrases.english: and if not, not.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, 'יבוקר' means checking whether an expert had permitted the animal, so ריש לקיש's view still stands.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יבוקר' means checking whether the blemish is permanent, so no expert is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יבוקר' means checking whether an expert permitted it, so an expert is still required.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה rejects the Babylonian reading
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports this discussion to רבי ירמיה, who sharply rejects it. He quotes רבי יוחנן: the argument in the ברייתא is about a case where someone searched for the blemished animal and did not find it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין went up to ארץ ישראל, he said this teaching before רבי ירמיה. רבי ירמיה said: Foolish Babylonians! Because they live in a dark land, they say dark teachings. Haven't they heard what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the argument is where someone searched and did not find?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. The Babylonian way of explaining the ברייתא is rejected, and a whole new reading is offered in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן had moved the ברייתא to a case about wool (step 9). רבי יוחנן keeps it about the blemished animals themselves, mixed into a flock. The argument is only where someone searched and still did not find the blemished one. This also answers the question from step 8: the תנא קמא forbids only when the animal was not found.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)
A dark land (a nickname for בבל)
He searched and did not find

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not arguing about the הלכה of wool. He is saying the ברייתא is not about wool at all. It is about the blemished animals themselves that got mixed into the flock.

phrases.english: When Ravin went up,
phrases.notes: He went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he said this teaching before Rabbi Yirmeya.
He said: Foolish Babylonians!
Because they live in a dark land,
they say teachings that are dark!
Have they not heard

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: that which Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is where he searched and did not find.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רָבִין, אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב נחמן's wool-based reading (step 9) and the back-and-forth built on it (steps 10-11).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole Babylonian explanation that the ברייתא is about wool
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is not needed. The ברייתא can be read simply as being about animals, in a case where someone searched and did not find.

steps.title: The argument matches רבי מאיר and the Rabbis on impurity
steps.stepSummary: The argument in the ברייתא follows the known dispute between רבי מאיר and רבנן. רבי מאיר holds that anything with a status of טומאה stays impure until the impurity is actually found.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue in the same dispute as רבי מאיר and רבנן. As we learned, רבי מאיר used to say: anything that had a status of טומאה stays impure forever, until the impurity is found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's case by linking it to an older dispute. It quotes רבי מאיר's side now; the next lines will bring the view of רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, a search that finds nothing does not remove a known problem. We assume the search was not done well. In the same way, the תנא קמא keeps the whole flock forbidden, because the blemished animal was never found.

phrases.english: And they disagree
in the dispute of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis,
as we learned, that Rabbi Meir would say:
Anything that was in a status of impurity
remains forever in its impurity,
until the impurity becomes known.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָמִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבָּנַן, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's case from step 12 by tying it to an existing dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a known status of טומאה stays in place until the impurity itself is found. A search that finds nothing does not remove it.

steps.title: The Rabbis: Dig until you reach untouched ground
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that if you search thoroughly, down to bedrock or untouched soil, and find nothing, the טומאה is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis say: He digs until he reaches bedrock or untouched soil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the dispute from the previous step by giving the view of the חכמים against רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said טומאה stays until it is actually found. The חכמים say that a full search that finds nothing is enough to treat it as gone. So in our ברייתא, the תנא קמא follows רבי מאיר (still forbidden), and רבי יוסי follows the חכמים (permitted after searching).

keyTerms.meaning: Untouched soil that was never dug up

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1 of רבי יוחנן: searched and did NOT find. תנא קמא = רבי מאיר (forbidden). רבי יוסי = חכמים (permitted).

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
He digs until he reaches
bedrock or untouched soil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וחכמים אומרים חופר עד שמגיע לסלע או לבתולה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבי מאיר / חכמים dispute that was started in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thorough search that finds nothing is enough to treat the טומאה as gone.

steps.title: A second version: He searched and found
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן differently: the ברייתא is about a case where he searched and found a blemished animal, and it matches the dispute of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The dispute is where he checked and found, and they argue about the same thing that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what רבי יוחנן said about the ברייתא. It is setting up the source for this version in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, nothing was found. Here, a blemished animal WAS found. The question is whether we may assume the one we found is the same one that was lost.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The dispute is where he checked and found,
and they argue about the dispute
of Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אסי אמר רבי יוחנן מחלוקת כשבדק ומצא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of רבי יוחנן's explanation than the one given in steps 12-14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא is about a case where a blemished animal was found, and it follows the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The lost grave in a field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if a grave is lost in a field, anyone entering is impure. If a grave is later found, רבי says we assume it is the lost one. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the whole field must be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A field where a grave was lost, one who enters it is impure. If a grave was found in it, one who enters it is pure, because I say the grave that was lost is the grave that was found. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: The whole field must be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says that once a grave is found, we may assume it is the lost one, so the rest of the field is pure. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we cannot assume that, and we must check everything. In our ברייתא, the תנא קמא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (still forbidden), and רבי יוסי follows רבי (permitted, since the found animal is the lost one).

keyTerms.meaning: A field in which a grave was lost
For I say, meaning we may assume

steps.whatToRemember: Version 2 of רבי יוחנן: searched and FOUND. תנא קמא = רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (check everything, forbidden). רבי יוסי = רבי (the found one is the lost one, permitted).

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
A field in which a grave was lost,
one who enters it is impure.
If a grave was found in it,
one who enters it is pure,
because I say:
the grave that was lost
is the grave that was found.
These are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
The entire field must be checked.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא שדה שאבד בה קבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source ברייתא for the dispute mentioned in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a found grave is assumed to be the lost one. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the whole field must be checked.

steps.title: Why did רבי אסי not accept the first version?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אסי did not explain the ברייתא like רבי חייא בר אבא, who said it was about searching and not finding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אסי, what is the reason he did not say like רבי חייא בר אבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אסי chose his own version instead of the first one. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version compared the ברייתא to the case of lost טומאה that was searched for and not found. The גמרא wants to know what was wrong with that comparison in רבי אסי's eyes.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Asi, what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא?
phrases.english: he did not say like Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba?
phrases.notes: רבי חייא בר אבא is the one behind the first version: searched and did not find.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי אסי מאי טעמא לא אמר כרבי חייא בר אבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions and asks why רבי אסי rejected the first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What flaw did רבי אסי see in the 'searched and did not find' explanation?

steps.title: A blemished animal cannot just disappear
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי would say: lost טומאה can be carried off by a raven or mouse, but a blemished animal in a flock has nowhere to go.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: It makes sense with טומאה. Say a raven came and took it, or a mouse came and took it. But here, where would the blemished animal go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אסי did not accept the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טומאה, it makes sense to say that a search which finds nothing means it is gone, because an animal could have carried it away. A blemished animal mixed into a flock cannot vanish like that. So a case of 'searched and did not find' makes no sense here.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
It makes sense regarding impurity,
say a raven came and took it,
or a mouse came and took it,
but here,
where would the blemished animal go?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לך בשלמא גבי טומאה אימר בא עורב ונטלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison to lost טומאה fails, because a blemished animal cannot be carried away the way a small impure item can.

steps.title: Maybe the blemish healed
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא would answer that the blemish may have been temporary and healed, which is why no blemished animal is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? Say it was a temporary blemish and it healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי חייא בר אבא would defend his version against רבי אסי's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal did not leave the flock. Its blemish went away, so it now looks like all the others. That explains how a search could find no blemished animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (how would he answer)?

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions stand. רבי אסי says a blemished animal cannot vanish, so it must be 'searched and found.' רבי חייא בר אבא says the blemish may have healed, so 'searched and not found' still works.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how would רבי חייא בר אבא answer this?

phrases.english: Say it was a temporary blemish and it healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואידך אימר מום עובר הוה ואיתסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the first version against the argument of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting how the blemished animal could be 'missing'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A blemished animal cannot disappear from a flock, so 'searched and not found' makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blemish may have been temporary and healed, so the animal is there but no longer looks blemished.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי חייא בר אבא explain it like רבי אסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around and asks why רבי חייא בר אבא did not use רבי אסי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why didn't רבי חייא בר אבא explain the ברייתא the way רבי אסי did?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier the גמרא asked why רבי אסי disagreed with רבי חייא בר אבא. Now it asks the opposite question. This line sets up רבי חייא בר אבא's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי linked the ברייתא to the argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about a lost grave. The גמרא wants to know why רבי חייא בר אבא did not accept that link. He explained the case as one where they searched and found nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not say like (someone else's explanation)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי אַסִּי?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rabbi Asi?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the question of step 17, now asking about the other אמורא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי חייא בר אבא rejected רבי אסי's reading, which tied the ברייתא to the lost-grave dispute.

steps.title: A field often has many graves, but checked animals don't suddenly get blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says the grave case is different. Fields normally hold many graves, but קדשים that were checked and found whole do not normally become blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: A field makes sense, because people are normally buried there. Just as this person was buried there, someone else may have been buried there too. But with קדשים that were checked and found whole, is it normal for them to suddenly get a blemish?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא explains why the lost-grave argument does not fit the case of the animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries that the grave they found might be a different one, because fields are used for burial. With animals that were checked and found whole, a new blemish is not expected. So even the stricter opinion would agree that the blemished animal they found is the same one. That is why רבי חייא בר אבא explained the ברייתא as a case where they searched and found nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (in this case)
Its normal way, what usually happens

phrases.english: He would say to you: Granted, a field,
it is normal to bury people in it,
so just as this one was buried in it,
another person may have been buried there.
But sacrificial animals,
since they were checked for us and stood whole,
is it normal for a blemish to fall on them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: בִּשְׁלָמָא שָׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grave case and the animal case are different: new graves in a field are expected, but new blemishes in checked animals are not, so the grave dispute does not apply.

steps.title: רבי אסי: animals gore each other, so blemishes are common
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers that animals butt each other with their horns, so new blemishes do happen often.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי אסי) would say: since they gore each other, blemishes are common among them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי defends his reading against רבי חייא בר אבא's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא said that a new blemish is unusual. רבי אסי disagrees: animals in a flock push and gore each other, so a new blemish is quite likely. That makes the animal case like the grave case, so the argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does fit.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים agree the question is whether a new blemish is likely. רבי חייא בר אבא says it is unusual. רבי אסי says it is common because animals gore each other.

phrases.english: And the other one: since they gore each other,
a blemish is common among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ אַגַּב דִּמְנַגְּחִי אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אסי's reply to רבי חייא בר אבא's reasoning in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual counter-claim: new blemishes are actually common.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Checked animals rarely get new blemishes, so the grave dispute does not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals gore each other, so new blemishes are common and the comparison to the grave case holds.

steps.title: Challenge from wool plucked off an unblemished בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: wool plucked from a בכור while it was unblemished stays forbidden, even if the animal later got a blemish and was slaughtered. The גמרא then starts to infer something from the word 'unblemished'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Someone who plucks wool from an unblemished בכור, even if it later got a blemish and he slaughtered it, the wool is forbidden. The reason is that it was unblemished...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי אסי's earlier statement, quoting רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, about the wool of a בכור. It quotes the ברייתא and begins an inference, which continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי said in the name of רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ that everyone agrees the wool is forbidden if an expert did not permit the בכור before the wool came off. The ברייתא forbids wool plucked while the animal was unblemished. The words 'טַעְמָא דְּתָם' set up a 'but if' inference: the reason is that it was unblemished, which suggests that wool plucked after the blemish might be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal with no blemish
The reason is that... (the opening of an inference)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished here. 'טַעְמָא דְּתָם' only starts the inference, and the 'but if it had a blemish' part comes next.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם
phrases.english: even though a blemish later developed in it
and he slaughtered it, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: It is the wool that stays forbidden.

phrases.english: The reason is that it was unblemished,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַתּוֹלֵשׁ צֶמֶר מִבְּכוֹר תָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the two explanations and goes back to challenge רבי אסי's statement in the name of רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ about a בכור's wool.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's statement in the name of רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ that the wool is forbidden unless an expert permitted the בכור before the wool came off.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא ties the prohibition to the animal being unblemished when plucked. That suggests wool plucked after a blemish appeared is allowed, even without an expert's permission.
